parsed.rationale: All 16 participating records are `type-alias-object` declarations with empty `fields_or_signature` lists and a `shared_field_count` of 1, meaning the only shared structural signal is that they are all type aliases — not that they alias the same underlying type or encode the same concept. The names are entirely unrelated domain concepts: `ConfettiView`, `DebugHUD`, `DialADJPage`, `HeightReader`, `InfoDetailView`, `PlaycutLoadingSection`, `TalksetView`, `WXYCLogo`, etc., spread across six distinct packages (`DebugPanel`, `WXUI`, `Wallpaper`, `PartyHorn`, `PlayerHeaderView`, `MusicShareKit`) and two app targets (`app:WatchXYC`, `app:iOS`). The structural coincidence is purely that each file happens to declare a SwiftUI `typealias` (a common SwiftUI preview or view-alias pattern); there is no shared semantic content to extract, consolidate, or generalize. Lifting any of these into a common location would couple unrelated domain modules for no benefit.
